desk.headline: Revenue up 19% to $10.6m, above estimates; loss narrows to 13c a share; no financial guidance, ABCL635 late-stage start set for 2027

other.label: Cash and marketable securities
other.change: total liquidity over $890m incl. government funding

results: Revenue rose 19% to $10.6m, almost all from research fees; licensing and royalty income was only $0.1m.
Net loss narrowed to $40.8m (13c a share) from $57.1m (19c) as R&D fell 21% to $43.5m and SG&A fell 45% to $13.6m.
A $200m share and pre-funded warrant offering (about $189m net) lifted cash and marketable securities above $790m; total liquidity tops $890m with government funding.
Operating cash flow for the nine months was a $19.3m inflow, against a $96.6m outflow a year earlier, helped by $66m of deferred revenue.
Partner-led programs with an AbCellera stake fell to 34 from 44 at end-2025; 12 molecules with a stake are in the clinic.

guidance.summary: AbCellera gives no revenue or earnings guidance. It expects to start late-stage development of ABCL635 for menopausal hot flashes in 2027, with 12-week and extension data due early 2027.

points: ABCL635 Phase 2: hot-flash frequency fell 83% vs 33% on placebo at week 4, with no serious or severe side effects on drug.
ABCL635 is being widened to hot flashes caused by breast and prostate cancer hormone treatment, with trials expected in 2027.
ABCL992, a longer-acting follow-on to ABCL635, plus ABCL385 and ABCL646 entered IND-enabling work.
ABCL575 met its Phase 1 goals (half-life about 65 days), but AbCellera does not plan to develop it past Phase 1.
Management said all 2026 corporate priorities have been delivered.
call.source: Q3 2026 business update slides (Exhibit 99.2) and press release; no independent call coverage found

watch: ABCL635 12-week and open-label extension data, due early 2027.
Regulator feedback and the start date and cost of late-stage ABCL635 trials.
Further decline in partner-led programs, which fell from 44 to 34 this year.
